senses.gloss: (privative of יש; cmp. יָשִׁישׁ) to be weak, slender, old.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 32a:18-28">Ber. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>עכשיו … ת׳ כחו כנקבה</he> now the nations will say, his (God’s) power has grown weak as that of a woman.

<cite ref="Pesachim 62b:15">Pes. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>מיום … ת׳ כחן וכ׳</he> from the day that the Book of Genealogy was suppressed, the strength of the wise has failed, and the light of their eyes has grown dim.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:1">Esth. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>ותַשׁ</he>, v. <cite ref="T01122"><he>רָתַח</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Menachot 29b:4">Men. 29ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="V01079"><he>תָּשׁוּשׁ</he></cite>; pl. <he>תְּשׁוּשִׁים</he>, <he>תְּשׁוּשִׁין</he>.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:18">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 17</cite> <he>מה … הת׳ וכ׳</he> what did the feeble (old) among them (that crossed the Red Sea) do?; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 161:3">Yalk. Sam. 161</cite> <he>הת׳ והפודגרין</he> the feeble and the lame.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:16">Cant. R. to V, 16</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 29:4">Ps. XXIX, 4</cite>) <he>קול ה׳ בכח לבחורים … לת׳</he> (not <he>לתשי׳</he>) ‘the voice of the Lord with strength’—for the youths; ‘the voice of the Lord with majesty’—for the feeble; (<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10">Num. R. s. 10<sup>1</sup></cite> <he>לַתַּשִּׁים</he>); a. e.
Snh. 26ᵇ (play on תושיה, Is. XXVIII, 29) למה נקרא … שמַתֶּשֶׁת כחו וכ׳ why is the law called tushiyah? Because the study of it weakens the strength of man (v. תַּשְׁיוּתָא).
<cite ref="Gittin 70a:20">Gitt. 70ᵃ</cite> <he>שלשה דברים מַתִּישִׁין וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>מתיזין</he>) three things weaken man’s strength; a. e.
